entity_resolution.canonical_name: Abu Rayhan Muhammad ibn Ahmad al-Biruni
entity_resolution.arabic_name: أبو الريحان محمد بن أحمد البيروني
entity_resolution.nationality_context: Khwarazmian Persian scholar of the Islamic Golden Age

importance_evaluation.scientific_significance: Pioneered early geodetic measurement techniques using trigonometric methods to determine the Earth's radius; advanced experimental hydrostatics by inventing specialized apparatus to determine specific gravities of metals and minerals; made significant contributions to astronomy, spherical trigonometry, and mechanics.
importance_evaluation.historical_significance: One of the prominent polymaths of the Islamic Golden Age; authored seminal comparative texts on Indian culture and science (Kitab al-Hind); bridged Greek, Indian, and Islamic scientific traditions.

timeline_a_biological.event: Born in Kath, capital of the Afrighid dynasty of Khwarazm.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Recorded in primary historical biographical notes and al-Biruni's own writings.

timeline_a_biological.event: Left Khwarazm following political upheaval and civil conflict, traveling to Rayy.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Documented in al-Biruni's astronomical observations recorded during this period.

timeline_a_biological.event: Resided at the Ziyarid court of Qabus ibn Ma'ali in Jurjan.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Dedicated 'The Remaining Signs of Past Centuries' to Qabus.

timeline_a_biological.event: Moved to Ghazna under the patronage (and political detention) of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Well-documented historical campaign of Mahmud in Khwarazm.

timeline_a_biological.event: Died in Ghazna (in modern-day Afghanistan) at around age 75.
timeline_a_biological.evidence_note: Exact date varies between 1048 and 1050 CE in historical sources.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Observed a lunar eclipse in Kath synchronously with Abu al-Wafa in Baghdad to calculate the longitude difference between the two cities.
Completed 'al-Athar al-Baqiyya' (The Remaining Signs of Past Centuries), a comprehensive comparative treatise on calendars, eras, and chronology.
Executed trigonometric measurement of Earth's radius at Fort Nandana in the Punjab region.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Detailed in 'Al-Qanun al-Mas'udi' and 'Tahdid Nihayat al-Amakin'.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Completed 'Tahqiq ma lil-Hind' (Kitab al-Hind), an exhaustive study of Indian culture, religion, mathematics, and astronomy.
Completed 'Al-Qanun al-Mas'udi' (The Mas'udic Canon), an extensive astronomical encyclopedia dedicated to Sultan Mas'ud.
timeline_b_scientific.evidence_note: Major surviving work of Islamic astronomy.

timeline_b_scientific.description: Authored 'Kitab al-Jamahir fi Ma'rifat al-Jawahir', detailing hydrostatic measurements of specific gravities of metals and gemstones.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Geodetic Determination of Earth's Radius via Horizon Dip
physics_analysis.historical_claim: Calculated the radius of the Earth using a single mountain height measurement combined with the dip angle of the horizon, bypassing long distance land surveys.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Determining Earth's physical curvature/radius without undertaking expansive, labor-intensive terrestrial arc measurements across flat terrain.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: The angle of dip of the horizon observed from a mountain of known height allows calculation of the radius of a spherical Earth using planar right-triangle trigonometry.
physics_analysis.historical_model_or_framework: Spherical Earth geometry operating within classical Euclidean geometric principles.
physics_analysis.modern_interpretation: Trigonometric determination of Earth's mean radius using $R = \frac{h \cos\theta}{1 - \cos\theta}$, where $h$ is mountain height and $\theta$ is the horizon dip angle.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: At Fort Nandana, al-Biruni measured the height of a hill ($h$) using vertical angles from two ground points. He then climbed to the summit and measured the horizon dip angle (\theta) using an astrolabe/quadrant.

variables_definition.h: Height of the mountain above the surrounding plain
variables_definition.\\theta: Angle of dip of the horizon below the true horizontal

equations.validity_domain: Spherical Earth assumption with uniform line-of-sight sight lines.
equations.assumptions: Atmospheric refraction is neglected or negligible; Earth is perfectly spherical; mountain height is accurately known.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Yielded an Earth radius estimate (~6,339.6 km using standard cubit conversions) within ~0.5% to 1% of modern average Earth radius values (6,371 km).
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Extremely sensitive to small angular measurement errors in $\theta$ and atmospheric refraction, which bends light near the horizon.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Method explicitly recorded in *Al-Qanun al-Mas'udi* and *Tahdid Nihayat al-Amakin*.

physics_analysis.contribution_name: Experimental Determination of Specific Gravity with Hydrostatic Balance
physics_analysis.historical_claim: Constructed a specialized conical vessel ('al-makayil') to measure the volume of displaced water, enabling high-precision measurement of specific gravities of metals and minerals.
physics_analysis.scientific_problem: Measuring the density/purity of irregular solids (metals, gemstones) accurately without destroying samples.
physics_analysis.historical_hypothesis: The ratio of the weight of a solid in air to the weight of an equal volume of water displaced yields the material's specific gravity.
physics_analysis.experiment_details: Used a conical vessel filled to a spill spout; immersed a weighed solid, caught the displaced water, and weighed the water to compute volume/density ratios.

variables_definition.W_{\\text{air}}: Weight of sample measured in air
variables_definition.W_{\\text{water}}: Weight of sample submerged in water

equations.assumptions: Water density is consistent across trials; surface tension and trapped air bubbles do not significantly skew displacement.

physics_analysis.result_and_impact: Obtained specific gravity values for gold (19.05 vs 19.30 modern), mercury (13.58 vs 13.56 modern), copper, and iron with accuracy often exceeding 98%.
physics_analysis.limitations_and_boundary_conditions: Did not account for systematic temperature fluctuations affecting water density.
physics_analysis.verification_note: Detailed in *Kitab al-Jamahir fi Ma'rifat al-Jawahir*; verified in studies by E.S. Kennedy and Nader El-Bizri.

teachers: Abu Nasr Mansur ibn Ali ibn Iraq
students: Abu al-Hasan Ali ibn Isa al-Walwaliji

major_claims_audit.claim: Al-Biruni discovered that the Earth rotates on its axis.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Al-Biruni evaluated the hypothesis of Earth's diurnal rotation (proposed by Abu Sa'id al-Sijzi and Indian astronomers), concluding it was physically plausible and mathematically equivalent to celestial rotation, though he ultimately considered it an open question in physics rather than an established certainty.

major_claims_audit.claim: Al-Biruni calculated the radius of the Earth with unprecedented accuracy using mountain-top dip angle trigonometry.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Al-Biruni designed and executed an original trigonometric method using horizon dip angles from a mountain peak to estimate Earth's radius within ~1% of modern values.

major_claims_audit.claim: Al-Biruni is the father of geodesy and modern physics.
major_claims_audit.recommended_wording: Al-Biruni made foundational contributions to early geodesy and experimental hydrostatics; however, titles such as 'father of geodesy' are modern honorific anachronisms.

major_uncertainties: Exact linear conversion value of the medieval cubit (dhira') used by al-Biruni affects exact percentage error calculation for his Earth radius measurement.
Exact year of death (1048 vs 1050 CE).
high_risk_claims: Anachronistically claiming al-Biruni was a firm proponent of heliocentrism or definitive Earth rotation rather than acknowledging his open-minded epistemological analysis.
